about.statement: A first-year student learning to code, tinkering with local LLMs, and curious about how AI actually works.
about.bio: I’m Siddharth, a first-year undergraduate studying Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI/ML & AIE) in Bengaluru, India. I'm just getting started on my tech journey—learning Python programming, playing around with local LLMs using Ollama on my laptop, learning the basic concepts of RAG, and building websites with Astro and TypeScript along the way.

projects.title: Testing Local LLMs with Ollama
projects.overview: Set up Ollama on my own machine to experiment with running open-source models (like Llama and Mistral) locally. Wanted to see firsthand how prompts work, how fast models respond on my laptop, and what running AI locally feels like.
projects.challenge: Understanding hardware limits and seeing how system prompts guide model responses.
projects.showcaseAlt: Local LLM latency and token generation benchmark
projects.heroAlt: Ollama dark mode terminal running Llama 3.2 locally

projects.title: Learning RAG Concepts
projects.overview: Started learning about the concept of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)—how vector embeddings and text chunking allow an LLM to look up information from local documents or notes before answering questions, reducing hallucinations.
projects.challenge: Learning how text gets turned into vector numbers and how similarity search finds the right passages.
projects.coverAlt: RAG vector embeddings and semantic search flowchart

projects.title: Building This Website
projects.overview: Built my personal website using Astro to learn modern web development. Created both a fun casual digital garden and a clean professional portfolio page to practice components, styling, and Git version control.
projects.challenge: Learning how Astro components work, managing layouts, and getting comfortable with Git commits and pushes.
projects.coverAlt: VS Code editor with Astro component structure
projects.showcaseAlt: Astro production build audit and terminal output
projects.heroAlt: Astro and TypeScript IDE development environment

projects.title: Python Foundations & Scripts
projects.overview: Practicing basic programming logic, loops, functions, and simple data structures in Python. Writing small scripts to automate everyday tasks and building a solid foundation for upcoming college coursework.
projects.challenge: Building programming logic and learning how to debug errors step by step.
projects.coverAlt: Python algorithm functions and vector math script
projects.showcaseAlt: Python algorithm unit tests passing in terminal
projects.heroAlt: Python script calculating cosine similarity between embedding vectors

principles.title: Curious above all
principles.description: I'm just starting out, so staying curious, asking questions, and exploring new tools is my top priority.

principles.title: Learn by breaking things
principles.description: Concepts make sense to me when I install the tool, run the code, see it break, and figure out why.

principles.title: Keep it simple
principles.description: As a beginner, writing clean and readable code is way better than trying to make it unnecessarily complex.

principles.title: Embrace being a beginner
principles.description: Tech moves super fast, especially in AI. Being honest about what I know and eager to learn the rest is how I grow.

faq.a: I am a first-year undergraduate student pursuing Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI/ML & AIE) in Bengaluru, India.

faq.q: What have you experimented with so far?
faq.a: As a beginner, I like tinkering hands-on. I've set up Ollama to test running local LLMs on my laptop, read and learned about how RAG works to ground models with custom documents, and built this website using Astro to learn web development.

faq.q: What are your goals right now?
faq.a: My goal is to build strong programming fundamentals in Python and computer science, keep experimenting with AI tools, and collaborate on beginner-friendly projects or college hackathons.
Feel free to email me at siddharthmukherjee.cs@gmail.com or connect with me on GitHub. I'm always happy to talk tech and learn from others!
